title: The Fed just removed a 2027 rate decision — making the remaining 7 even more important
summary:
The Warsh Fed's taciturn nature has already raised the stakes for each FOMC meeting.
With fewer hints or forward guidance about what the Fed is thinking and planning comes more suspense.
At the October policy meeting on Wednesday, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh announced this major change to the Fed's calendar and added that 2028 might feature only six rate decisions.
"I don't believe in forward guidance," Warsh said on Wednesday.
His remarks echoed his move earlier this year to end the years-long practice of offering forward guidance — removing an important signal for Wall Street and Main Street alike.

title: Fed votes in split decision to hold interest rates steady despite sticky inflation
summary:
With the midterm elections less than a week away, the Federal Reserve held interest rates steady on Wednesday, even as the latest inflation reports show prices rising again.
The central bank voted in a split decision to hold its benchmark interest rate steady in the range of 3.75% to 4%, after raising rates last month for the first time in more than three years.
Cleveland Fed president Beth Hammack and Fed governor Lisa Cook broke ranks, preferring to raise rates by a quarter percentage point.
This is the second time since July Hammack has dissented in favor of raising rates and Cook's first dissent in her tenure.

title: How Aldi is pushing down grocery prices
summary:
It's the only time I've lived near Aldi, the grocery store known for low prices.
Sponsor MessageAldi is a German company known for having low, low prices, and it deserves that reputation.
All to say: Aldi is disrupting the grocery business and actually lowering prices even as the cost of food—at restaurants and other grocery stores—goes up and up.
Aldi unbundled the part of the grocery business it can do super cheaply, and it intentionally locates Aldi stores near competitor grocery stores so shoppers can easily go grab the last few things on their list (the rest of the bundle).
I think the way Aldi's growth pressured competitors to keep prices low shows that grocers are not the right target of our ire over food prices.
